text:
sam: Hey team, just started today 🎉. On an M2 Mac and also spinning up WSL for a linux parity environment. Followed the quickstart but hitting a couple issues: ruby and some npm native modules fail during compile (openssl / missing pkg-config), and my kube context isn't picked up by local k8s scripts. Also unsure where to stash REDWOOD_API_KEY locally. who should I bug for a minimal local env checklist?

toni: welcome! short checklist that helped me: install Homebrew (/opt/homebrew), asdf, direnv. On mac make sure openssl@3 is installed via brew and export the flags before building Ruby or gems. Example:
```bash
brew install openssl@3 pkg-config
export LDFLAGS=\"-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib\"
export CPPFLAGS=\"-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include\"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=\"/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig\"
# then asdf install ruby <version>
```
For WSL (Ubuntu) do `sudo apt install -y build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev pkg-config` first.

sam: thanks — what about node modules that call into Rust or native libs? i saw errors referencing cargo.

toni: install rustup (`curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh`) and ensure `~/.cargo/bin` is on PATH. For image-processing modules also install `libvips` on linux.

sam: and env vars / secrets? where do devs put REDWOOD_API_KEY locally?

toni: do NOT commit secrets. we use direnv + a local config path by convention: `~/.config/redwood/env.local` (not in git). Put exports there and `source_env` from `.envrc`. Sample: 
```bash
# ~/.config/redwood/env.local
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-local-xxxx
export REDWOOD_ENV=dev
export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config-redwood
```
You can also use `vault` integration if you need short-lived creds; ops can help.

sam: how do i get kubeconfig for the dev cluster?

cloudops: ping cloudops here — we provision a per-user kube context when you request access. Use the onboarding form (pinned in #new-hires) or DM me. When you get the file, place it at `~/.kube/config-redwood` and set `KUBECONFIG` to point to it, or merge with `~/.kube/config` using `kubectl config view --raw` instructions.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-4902 for sam - cloudops to provision kube access.

sam: awesome. any preferred dotfiles or handy snippets to copy?

toni: we have a starter dotfiles repo: https://github.com/redwood-onboarding/dotfiles-starter (ASDF init, direnv hooks, zsh aliases). Clone and copy what you need. If you want the company standard dotfiles synced, request access via infra. Also add `asdf` init lines to your shell rc: 
```bash
. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh
eval \"$(direnv hook zsh)\"
```

sam: last one — ssh key type? i made ed25519. is that ok?

cloudops: ed25519 is preferred. Add the public key to GitHub, then fill the onboarding form to request org access. For deploy keys, infra will instruct if we need to add to specific services.

sam: thanks y'all, i'll try the openssl flags + rustup and post logs if anything else breaks :thumbsup:
